summary: Saved annotations tied to revoked API keys included in scheduled CSV/PDF exports
description:
Issue summary: A Beacon Health Tech admin reported that scheduled dashboard exports (CSV and PDF) produced last week contain annotations that were created by API keys which the customer had already revoked.

Observed behavior: Saved annotations and their metadata (creator identifier and route) created with revoked API keys are still present in scheduled export files generated after the revocation. Annotations are visible in the exported artifacts but not visible in the customer console UI for the same time range and dashboard.

Expected behavior: Exports should only include annotations that are currently visible to the org (i.e., annotations created by active users or active API keys or annotations that have not been soft-deleted/expired) and must respect API key revocations and annotation retention policies.
impact: Customer reports potential exposure of historical annotation metadata tied to revoked credentials. This is a privacy/security concern for enterprise customers and may contravene their internal compliance rules. A single customer impacted so far, scheduled exports produced nightly for 10+ dashboards. No evidence of leaked PII in annotations yet but metadata (api_key_id, creator) is present.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create API key (api-key-xyz) and use it to POST annotations on dashboard A via console exporthook for time range T-1d.
2) Revoke API key via Console > Settings > API keys (immediately mark revoked).
3) Wait for next scheduled export run for dashboard A (nightly job).
4) Download the generated CSV/PDF and inspect annotations section; revoked api-key-created annotations appear in the export although they are not visible when viewing the dashboard in the UI.
5) Compare annotations list via API /annotations endpoint (filtered by active=true) and exported file — mismatch observed.

export-service join query preview: SELECT a.id, a.creator_id, a.api_key_id, a.visible FROM annotations a LEFT JOIN api_keys k ON a.api_key_id = k.id WHERE a.dashboard_id = 'dash-789' AND a.ts BETWEEN ...

note: in preview query results, rows with k.state = 'revoked' still returned because annotations table stores api_key_id and export pipeline does not re-evaluate key state; TTL cleanup job is scheduled weekly (ttl-annotations-cleanup).
comments: 2026-03-05 09:12 - Aisha Patel: Customer first reported at 08:55 via support email. Customer attached examples (two nightly CSVs and one PDF). They flagged api_key ids in CSV (api-key-xyz) which were revoked on 2026-03-03.

2026-03-05 10:00 - Marco Li: Acknowledged, triaged to exports/component. Marking P2 due to security/enterprise tier. Investigating whether scheduled job uses a cached snapshot of annotations or stale join.

2026-03-05 16:43 - Devon Reyes (SRE): Found that export pipeline runs a batch read against the annotations materialized table 'annotations_mv' — materialized view is refreshed hourly and only removed entries during weekly TTL cleanup. Hypothesis: annotations created by revoked api keys persist in annotations_mv until cleanup and export job does not check api key state.

2026-03-06 09:30 - Marco Li: Reproduced in staging by creating and revoking a key and verifying scheduled export produced the annotation. Added temporary filter to export query to exclude annotations whose api_key_id now maps to a revoked key. Patch in testing.

2026-03-07 11:05 - Security (Dana Cohen): Recommended conservative mitigation: mask api_key_id column in exports until fix deployed and run backfill to regenerate exports for affected orgs. Customer prefers removal rather than masking.
investigation_notes: 1) Root cause hypothesis: Export pipeline relies on a materialized view (annotations_mv) for performance. The MV retains annotation rows referencing api_key_id values even after keys are revoked because revocation state is in api_keys table and MV is not refreshed on key update. Scheduled export job queries annotations_mv without joining to api_keys table to check current state. Thus revoked-key annotations are exported until ttl-cleanup refresh removes them.

2) Secondary issue: scheduled-export job uses snapshot timestamp semantics (snapshot_ts = job_start - 5m) which allowed a race where recent revocations were not visible to the snapshot read window, compounding the MV staleness.
3) Frequency: Confirmed with export logs — affected runs from 2026-03-03 to 2026-03-05 (until temporary patch applied in staging).

4) Security assessment: annotations do not include PII in supplied examples, but api_key identifiers and creator_uuid are present and considered sensitive for customers with strict credential handling policies.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: Added export query predicate to join with api_keys and only include annotations where api_keys.state = 'active' OR annotations.api_key_id IS NULL. This was deployed to staging and validated against Beacon's sample.

Planned permanent fix: 1) Update export-service to always join live api_keys table and avoid relying solely on annotations_mv for security-sensitive fields. 2) Reduce annotations_mv refresh window for orgs with scheduled exports to near-real-time or implement change-propagation for api_key state updates. 3) Run a one-off backfill job to regenerate exports for orgs with scheduled-export runs during revocation window (2026-03-02 -> 2026-03-05).

Rollout notes: Patch PR #4876 merged, deployed to staging 2026-03-06, smoke-tested; targeted prod rollout 2026-03-08 after canary verification. Backfill job planned for 2026-03-09; progress is tracked in linked PR/Job run.

Customer follow-up: Beacon Health Tech requested confirmation when backfill completes and asked for an audit snapshot of all exports that included revoked api_key ids.
